title: FINAL FORMATION · SINGAPORE SEND-OFF
vibe: green · 30 minutes flat · a smoke session · last workout before the long haul home
why: Seven hours of sleep, nothing sore, thirty minutes, and you want it intense. Green, and this is the last session Singapore gets. The shape rotates hard: Sunday was a chipper, Monday a chain of ladders, yesterday the gauntlet — so today is the one clock this program has never actually run as the headline, a straight EMOM, and the tradition behind it is one this log has never once drawn from: military PT. The organizing idea is the smoke session — lots of reps, low rest, the clock owns you. Eighteen minutes, three stations on rotation, and the minute never cares how you feel. It headlines the two qualities that have gone quietest: the heavy front squat, untouched since the Anvil four days ago, and the snatch, silent for a week — and every snatch today starts DEAD from the floor, no backswing, which has never appeared in this log. Push-ups sit in the middle because no send-off in Army clothing goes home without them. Then 800 meters hard for the last run on this belt, and the program's first-ever Tabata to close. Thirty minutes. Every one of them works.

blocks.title: WARM-UP · DAY B · ANKLES, KNEES, SHOULDERS
blocks.meta: ~4 min · Moves Method Day B · ONE PASS · brisk, this is a 30-minute day

items.name: KNEES AND ANKLES · one pass
items.detail: Toe squats 30 sec · ankle rolls in a deep squat, 8 per direction · knee drives 8 per side · single-leg squat to a bench or bed edge, 5 per side. The heavy front squats come first on the clock, so the knees and ankles open first.

items.name: SHOULDERS · one pass
items.detail: Shoulder dislocates with a towel ×12 · shoulder extensions behind the back 30 sec · 10 scap push-ups from the knees. Ninety push-ups and seventy-two overhead snatches are coming. Prime the scaps, don't stretch them to sleep.

blocks.text: Day B off the Moves Method menu — Day A ran yesterday, Day C on Monday. Compressed to four minutes because the thirty belongs to the clock.

blocks.title: BLOCK 1 · THE SMOKE SESSION · 18-MIN EMOM
blocks.meta: 18 MINUTES · 6 CYCLES of 3 stations · 2 × 22 kg DB · 20 kg KB · bodyweight
blocks.format: EMOM · every minute on the minute, 3 stations rotating · effort measured in minutes HELD, not rounds chosen
blocks.workRest: On each top-of-minute, do the work; whatever is left of the minute is your rest. Miss the reps inside the minute and you don't stop — you just inherit a shorter rest. 18 minutes, no pause button.

items.name: MINUTE 1 · DOUBLE FRONT SQUAT · 2 × 22 kg DB × 6
items.detail: Both dumbbells in the rack, full-depth squat, stand all the way up. Six reps. This is the heaviest double-implement load in your log and the squat has been quiet since the Anvil — six clean reps should take ~25 seconds and leave you ~35 to breathe.

items.name: MINUTE 2 · PUSH-UPS × 15
items.detail: Chest to the deck, full lockout, body a plank the whole way. Fifteen unbroken if they're there, 10+5 if not. The Army staple, in an Army-shaped session, on your last day overseas. 90 total across the six cycles.

items.name: MINUTE 3 · ★ WILDCARD · DEAD-START SNATCH · 20 kg × 6 PER SIDE
items.detail: First dead-start snatch anywhere in this log. The bell starts DEAD on the floor every single rep — no backswing, no rebound. Grip, hike nothing: pull it from stillness straight to overhead lockout in one movement, park it, repeat. Six per side, twelve per minute. Killing the stretch reflex makes every rep a pure hip-and-lat produce-force-from-zero problem, and 72 of them is the biggest snatch volume in three weeks.

items.name: THE STANDARD · 6 FULL CYCLES = 18 MINUTES
items.detail: GREEN target: all 18 minutes at full written reps — 36 heavy front squats, 90 push-ups, 72 dead snatches, 198 reps. If every minute is landing with 20+ seconds of slack by cycle 3, the ceiling is open: take the last cycle at 7 squats / 18 push-ups / 7 per side. Tell me which version you ran.

blocks.noteGreen: Seeded from Neupert's double-grind pairings (#69 '2G 1' family) restructured onto a 3-station rotating EMOM — the smoke-session clock is the day's engine. Written at the top of the range on purpose.
blocks.text: The EMOM is the one dominant format this program has somehow never headlined. The military-PT idea it carries: high reps, short rest, and the clock — not your preference — decides when you work.

blocks.title: BLOCK 2 · THE LAST SINGAPORE RUN · 800 m HARD
blocks.meta: ~4 min · ONE EFFORT · 13.5–14.0 km/h on this belt
blocks.format: single hard run effort · straight off the EMOM, compromised legs

items.name: 800 m · 13.5–14.0 km/h · one piece
items.detail: Step on within two minutes of the last snatch — this is a gauntlet-style compromised leg, deliberately. On this belt anything ≥13 is hard, so 13.5–14 for 800 m is a real closing effort, roughly 3:30 of work. Cadence high and light, ~170 steps a minute. This machine has been sandbagging its numbers at you for two weeks; leave it with your hardest 800 of the block.

items.name: 📋 STILL OWED · a watch split
items.detail: If the watch is on, give me distance + average pace for this 800. The Singapore belt leaves the log uncalibrated unless today closes it out.

blocks.text: Your own two-miler is always yours — if the day has room outside these thirty minutes, run it. Inside the thirty, this 800 is the run.

blocks.title: BLOCK 3 · TABATA MIDLINE · FIRST TABATA IN THE PROGRAM
blocks.meta: 4 MINUTES · 8 ROUNDS of 20 sec work / 10 sec rest · bodyweight
blocks.format: Tabata · 8 × 20/10 · alternating two movements · ★ first use of this format anywhere in the log
blocks.workRest: 20 seconds on, 10 seconds off, 8 rounds, done. Alternate the two movements: odd rounds hollow rocks, even rounds plank shoulder taps.

items.name: ODD ROUNDS · HOLLOW ROCKS · 20 sec
items.detail: Low back pressed into the floor, arms by ears, rock small and tight. If the low back peels up, bend the knees — position beats amplitude. Anti-extension, the one midline quality not touched this week.

items.name: EVEN ROUNDS · PLANK SHOULDER TAPS · 20 sec
items.detail: High plank, feet wide, tap the opposite shoulder without the hips swaying a degree. Anti-rotation under fatigue, right after the hollow has cooked the front line.

blocks.text: Monday's midline was loaded lateral flexion, yesterday's was loaded anti-rotation — today closes anti-extension, on the one clock format the program has never used. Four minutes, honest ones.

blocks.title: COOLDOWN · 2 MIN

items.name: WALK + BREATHE · 90 sec
items.detail: Belt at 5 km/h or just pace the floor. Nose breathing, long exhales. You have a long-haul flight ahead — start the downshift now.

items.name: DOORWAY PEC + DEEP SQUAT HOLD · 30 sec
items.detail: Open the chest after 90 push-ups, sit the hips into a deep squat after 36 heavy ones. Hips and chest are what the airplane seat will attack — leave them long.

blocks.text: That's Singapore. See you on the Bowflex.
